ca_hueco_wall_2.blurb: Hueco Wall is a sport crag in Box Canyon East, part of the New Jack City zone in the High Desert near Barstow. It has nine bolted routes, three at 5.10 and six at 5.11, so it suits climbers working at those levels rather than beginners. The wall faces west, and the lines run from vertical to gently overhanging, with a sustained, pumpy feel. Because the grades sit in a narrow band, it works well as a focused session for someone already comfortable leading in the 5.10s who wants a few steady 5.11 attempts without much walking between climbs.

ca_inner_sanctum_2.blurb: Inner Sanctum is a tight, corridor-like crag within the Tatooine group on Fairview Mountain, in the High Desert at Apple Valley. It sits just behind the Jabba crag and is entered either through a tunnel on Jabba's left or by scrambling over boulders. Nine routes mix five sport lines with four trad lines, running from about 5.8 to 5.12 with most falling around 5.9 and 5.10. The granodiorite walls are close together, and the trad side includes an offwidth. A good stop for a climber who wants moderate to mid-grade variety in a very compact setting.

ca_jabba.blurb: Jabba is a crag in the Tatooine group on Fairview Mountain, at Apple Valley in California's High Desert, and it is among the first crags met on the walk in. A large brown granodiorite block dominates the spot. Nine climbs include six sport routes from about 5.5 to 5.10, one trad line at 5.8+, and two boulder problems at the easy end. Most of the bolted routes are friendly mid-grade lines, which makes it a handy place for newer leaders and for warming up before heading to the harder walls nearby.

ca_iron_man_boulder.blurb: Iron Man Boulder is a compact bouldering spot in Buttermilk Country, in the Bishop area of the Eastern Sierra. It stands a short walk past Hero Roof Boulder and anchors a small cluster of boulders around it. Nine problems range from around V1 up to V8, with a handful in the V4 range and a few harder ones above V6. The best-known line is a traverse on the south-facing side. It suits a short session, with enough variety for climbers across a wide range of strength.

ca_lamont_pinnacles.blurb: Lamont Pinnacles is a trad crag on the southeastern edge of the Domeland Wilderness in the southern Sierra, set high above a Joshua tree-dotted desert basin. Nine routes climb pinnacles and aretes, with most of the longer ones running three to seven pitches. Grades are concentrated around 5.10, with one easier route near 5.8 and a single 5.12. The place sees few visitors and the days are committing, so it suits experienced parties who are comfortable placing their own gear and managing a multi-pitch objective.

ca_iris_slab.blurb: Iris Slab is a small slab crag at roughly 8,500 feet in Rock Creek, between Bishop and Mammoth Lakes in the Eastern Sierra. Guide schools have long used it to teach beginners. Nine routes run from about 5.5 to 5.10, most at 5.7 and 5.8, with a few harder ones near 5.10. The surface is slick and protection can be fiddly, so most climbers set up a single-rope top rope, often from bolts, rather than lead. It is a good first outing for newer climbers learning slab footwork.

ca_kaleidoscope_wall.blurb: Kaleidoscope Wall is a small trad crag in the Lost Horse part of Joshua Tree National Park, sitting partway up a hillside at around 4,800 feet. The rock is paler and more polished than most of the park, forming a grey, slabby face. Nine routes cover roughly 5.8 to 5.11, with the largest group at 5.10 and a pair at 5.11. Most of the climbing is moderate, and one of the 5.10 lines carries a runout rating. It works as a change of pace from the busier walls nearby.
